solutions.check: 32 entries; each light the paper's grid did not give solved here from its clue's wordplay (an anagram or hidden word, the one listed word fitting every crossing) and its definition (WordNet), agrees with the 31 answers the paper printed

clue.text: Handy treatment for my patient

parts.note: a care for the hands, and also, split up, a phrase saying 'the fellow I treat' — a doctor's patient

explanation.surface: A doctor describes a practical remedy given to someone in their care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handy' means 'for the hands' rather than 'convenient', and the answer split into three words gives 'man I cure', a fair description of my patient.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a cosmetic treatment of the hands and fingernails.

clue.text: A little time with the girls, they're sweet.

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a little time
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: A brief spell with some young women, who are lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they're sweet' looks like praise of the girls, but it is the definition of a sugary syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: This thick dark syrup from sugar refining is very sweet, and the word is treated as plural here.

clue.text: He supplies regular press hand-outs

parts.note: the press hand-outs are not publicity releases but newspapers handed over the counter daily

explanation.walkthrough: 'press hand-outs' suggests a publicist's releases, but the newspapers sold over a shop counter every day are meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper who sells daily papers and magazines provides the press on a regular basis.

clue.text: Goddess heard in sequence

indicators.note: the clue's word is spoken, giving the sound of a word for a sequence

parts.note: a series is a sequence

explanation.surface: A deity heard speaking in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceres was the Roman goddess of agriculture and grain.

clue.text: Literate town

definitions.meaning: literate here means able to read
A large town in Berkshire, west of London

explanation.surface: A well-educated place to live.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a large English town in Berkshire, west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who can read is literate, and Reading is an English town on the Thames.

clue.text: Stock melody

explanation.surface: A shop's goods set beside a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed or line of descent is a stock, and a tune or passage of music is likewise called this.

clue.text: An old custom perhaps to drain it?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that these letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Asking whether some ancient practice is to empty out a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges TO DRAIN IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradition is a long-held custom handed down through generations.

clue.text: Showing 11, drink about four

indicators.note: the drink goes about, around, the numeral that follows

parts.note: ale is a drink
IV is the Roman numeral for four

explanation.surface: Displaying something while having a beer around four o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 across's answer means liveliness, so showing it means full of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lively and full of vigour means showing spirit, as when someone is said to be truly living.

clue.text: Score after one's allotted time

parts.note: the Bible allots a lifespan of three score and ten; another score of twenty beyond that gives the figure

explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' looks like a sporting result but means twenty: the Bible's allotted span is threescore and ten, seventy years, and twenty more follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventy, the biblical span, plus a score of twenty makes this number.

clue.text: It's just the job for a commuter

definitions.text: It's just the job for a commuter

parts.words: It's just the job for a commuter
parts.note: 'just the job' is an idiom for exactly what is wanted, and a traveller to work needs a pass to ride

explanation.walkthrough: 'just the job' is British slang for exactly right, a sense the word shares with the pass a rail traveller buys.
explanation.definitionFit: 'That's the ticket' means exactly what's needed, and a commuter needs a travel pass of this kind.

clue.text: Become less neat

definitions.meaning: neat is an old word for cattle, so one that lows, a cow, fits

explanation.surface: Something that grows untidier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is not tidy but the old word for cattle; a lowing beast is one that moos.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop or diminish is one sense; the other reads the word as 'one that moos', a cow.

clue.text: I'm in a race-go !

indicators.note: the clue says these two letters sit inside the word for a race

parts.note: a race of people is a nation
I'm contracted to its letters

explanation.surface: An excited runner shouts that they are entered in a race and off they go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' looks like a starter's cry, but it is the definition, in its sense of energy or liveliness.
explanation.definitionFit: Go means vigour or liveliness, as does this word for spirited vivacity.

clue.text: Film in which a lot of pastry is thrown about

definitions.text: Film in which a lot of pastry is thrown about

parts.words: Film in which a lot of pastry is thrown about
parts.note: the pastry is custard pies hurled at faces in knockabout comedy, not a recipe being anagrammed

explanation.surface: A movie scene where dough gets tossed around a kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown about' and 'pastry' tempt an anagram, but the letters do not fit; it describes custard-pie comedy films.
explanation.definitionFit: Boisterous physical comedy with pratfalls and pie-throwing is this genre of film.

clue.text: Like gases carried in container transport

indicators.note: the letters are carried inside the phrase that follows, running across the two words

explanation.surface: Gas cylinders are shipped in freight containers.
explanation.definitionFit: The noble gases are called by this name because they react with almost nothing.

clue.text: Time of day when engine breaks down — about five

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the numeral that follows
an engine that breaks down falls apart, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A car fails at some hour, roughly five o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks down' turns ENGINE into EENING, and 'about' puts V inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The later part of the day, after afternoon, is a time of day.

clue.text: Wandering in it, aren't gypsies so described?

indicators.note: the words that follow wander from their order, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether travelling folk are called roamers because they are always on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wandering' looks like the definition, but it rearranges IN IT AREN'T.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling people who move from place to place are often called nomadic or wayfaring.

clue.text: Double back, for instance, in pain

parts.note: a twin is a double of someone

indicators.note: the abbreviation that follows is read back to front

explanation.surface: Someone bends over again and feels a pang, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double back' reads as a phrase meaning to turn round, but 'back' belongs with 'for instance', turning EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden sharp pang is a brief pain.

clue.text: In the main a characteristic transmitter to reassemble

parts.note: a gene transmits inherited characteristics
to rally is to reassemble troops

explanation.surface: At sea, a radio set typical of its kind is put back together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' suggests the open sea, but means mostly; 'reassemble' is not an anagram signal but the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: In the main and usually both mean for the most part.

clue.text: Help in twisting fibre remnant

indicators.note: twisting a thread winds it round, so the word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: an end is a remnant, as in an end of cloth

explanation.surface: Assisting with spinning a scrap of thread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisting' makes BEFRI from FIBRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be a friend to someone in need is to help them.

clue.text: Sign of rank of non-conforming priest

indicators.note: a priest who will not conform breaks ranks, so the word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The insignia worn by a dissenting cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: A chevron or band on a sleeve shows rank; the grid as held prints a D in the unchecked square, which neither definition nor wordplay supports.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe on the sleeve marks a soldier's grade, such as a corporal's two.

clue.text: Trepan, to, put it another way

definitions.text: Trepan, to, put it another way

parts.words: Trepan, to, put it another way
parts.note: trepan means to ensnare, and putting its letters another way gives a synonym

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trepan' looks like the surgeon's drill but is the old verb meaning to trick or lure; rearranging it also gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Trepan is an old verb meaning to lure or ensnare, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Expiation from last character leaving pirate stronghold

indicators.note: the last letter of the alphabet leaves the place name

parts.note: Penzance, the Cornish town of Gilbert and Sullivan's The Pirates of Penzance
Z is the last character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Atonement made by the final person to quit a buccaneers' base.
explanation.walkthrough: Penzance is a Cornish seaport made famous by the comic opera The Pirates of Penzance.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is an act of atonement for wrongdoing, which is what expiation means.

clue.text: Go ahead and get caught in deeper trouble

indicators.note: the cricket abbreviation goes inside the rearranged word
the word is in trouble, thrown into disorder

parts.note: c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Advance and find yourself stuck in even worse difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' makes PREEDE from DEEPER, and 'in' puts C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To come before is to go ahead of something.

clue.text: Titania's fairy trap

definitions.meaning: one of the fairies attending Titania in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: The queen of the fairies has a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: Titania is the fairy queen in A Midsummer Night's Dream; one of her attendant fairies is named after a spider's web.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider's web is a trap for insects, and Shakespeare named a fairy attendant after one.

clue.text: See cat jump off piano

indicators.note: the musical abbreviation is taken off the word for a jump

parts.note: to pounce is to jump on something
p is the musical marking for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Watch a feline leap off the keyboard instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piano' is not the instrument but the musical marking p, meaning softly.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard, a big cat of Central Asian mountains, is also called this.

clue.text: Elbow grease's first used in a form of sculpture

indicators.note: the letter is used inside the sculpture word

parts.note: a nude is an unclothed figure, a form of sculpture

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A sculptor's hard work goes first into a statue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elbow grease' reads as one phrase for hard work, but 'Elbow' is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To elbow someone is to push or prod them with the arm, as in a nudge.

clue.text: Wrongful arrest seizing waterway's Finance Officer

indicators.note: the rearranged letters grab and hold the river inside them
a wrongful arrest is a wrong one, so its letters are put in a different order

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A company's money man is unlawfully detained by police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrongful' makes TREASR from ARREST, and 'seizing' puts URE, a river, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer looks after the funds of a society or company.

clue.text: Cut, cut hard

indicators.note: the second cut shortens the word for hard by its last letter

parts.note: severe means hard or harsh

explanation.surface: Slash, slash viciously.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Cut' is the definition; the second docks the end of SEVERE.
explanation.definitionFit: To sever is to cut through or apart.

clue.text: Fly on ahead, say?

definitions.meaning: fly in slang means sharp or alert
read as 'on a head', something worn there, a hat: the name is also that of a broad-brimmed felt hat

explanation.surface: An instruction to a flier to go on in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' is the slang adjective for shrewd, not the verb; 'on ahead' splits into 'on a head', where a broad-brimmed felt hat of that name sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Fully alert people are hard to fool, like fly ones; and a soft felt hat with a wide brim has this name.

clue.text: Dance brought back by East European

indicators.note: the people named are read back to front

parts.note: a Slav is a member of a European people

explanation.surface: A dance number reintroduced by someone from Eastern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns SLAV into VALS, and E for East follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Valse is the French word for a waltz, a dance in triple time.

clue.text: All 7 draw it

parts.note: 7 down's answer means living, and everyone living takes in air, so draw it means inhale

explanation.walkthrough: 'draw' looks like sketching, but here it means inhaling: everything that is living draws air into its lungs.
explanation.definitionFit: Living creatures inhale air, so drawing this is what being living means.

clue.text: Seduced, Elizabeth was radiant

parts.note: Bet is a pet form of the name Elizabeth
rayed means shone out in rays, was radiant

explanation.surface: A woman named Elizabeth glowed after being charmed into bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead astray and abandon is one sense of seducing someone and of being false to them.
